sections.html: Nemapteryx nenga is a catfish from India, formerly placed in the genus Arius. It is not a shark, despite the name "freshwater shark". It reaches about 30 cm and should be kept in large aquariums only.
These "freshwater sharks" live in the mouths of large rivers, so they can live in pure freshwater as well as in pure seawater.
Keeping them in brackish water with a salt content of 5-10 grams per litre is recommended.
These catfish should always be kept in groups (5-10 specimens). Singly kept specimens do not thrive very well.
As far as is known, all species of the Arius relatives are mouthbrooders. The male takes the eggs into his mouth until they hatch.
Because of its nicely shaped dorsal fin, the popular name "whimple freshwater shark" could be used.
